channel.title: Brazil Elections 2026
channel.description: Real-time monitoring of the 2026 Brazilian presidential elections.

item.title: Tarcísio: operações de crédito do Amapá não ficam travadas; de SP, ficam
item.description: Tarcísio de Freitas defended the formation of a strong center-right bloc in the Senate and claimed that São Paulo is poorly represented in the House. Without mentioning Davi Alcolumbre, the governor compared Amapá, saying that credit operations from the state are not stalled like those of São Paulo.

item.title: Datafolha: Flávio Bolsonaro lidera disputa presidencial no DF
item.description: A Datafolha poll released on August 22nd shows Flávio Bolsonaro (PL) leading the presidential race among voters in the Federal District, with 39% of voting intentions, followed by Lula (PT) with 31% and Ronaldo Caiado (PSD) with 10%. In a scenario including Pablo Marçal (PRTB), Flávio has 37% and Lula maintains 31%, indicating that his inclusion does not significantly change the overall picture. The margin of error is three percentage points, with a 95% confidence level.

item.title: Eleições 2026: veja como está a corrida presidencial em SP, RJ, DF, MG, PE e PI, segundo o Datafolha
item.description: Datafolha polls released this Saturday (22) show the presidential race split across six Brazilian states. Flávio Bolsonaro (PL) leads in São Paulo, Rio de Janeiro, and the Federal District, while Lula (PT) is ahead in Pernambuco, Minas Gerais, and Piauí. In São Paulo, Flávio has 37% versus Lula's 33%, with Renan Santos (Missão) in third at 5%.

item.title: No RJ, Flávio marca 49% contra 40% de Lula em 2º turno, diz Datafolha
item.description: Datafolha poll shows Flávio Bolsonaro (PL) leading with 49% against Lula's (PT) 40% in a potential runoff in Rio de Janeiro. In the first round, Flávio leads 41% to 36%. Survey of 1,204 voters conducted Aug 18-20, with a 3-point margin of error.

item.title: Datafolha: veja os índices de popularidade de Lula em São Paulo, Minas, Rio, Pernambuco e DF
item.description: A Datafolha poll released on August 22, 2026, 43 days before the first round, shows Lula's decline in popularity in São Paulo, Rio de Janeiro, and the Federal District, where negative ratings exceed positive ones. In Minas Gerais the gap is narrower, while in Pernambuco the president enjoys majority approval. Nationally, Lula leads with 39% versus Flávio Bolsonaro's 33%, and would win a runoff 47% to 43%.

item.title: Kassab caminha para Lula no segundo turno, mas escorrega na lama do Lulinha
item.description: Kassab and the PSD are moving toward pro-Lula neutrality in the runoff, leveraging Caiado's 5% as bargaining power. According to Datafolha, Flávio Bolsonaro remains competitive against Lula (43% to 47%), while Caiado trails. The scenario, however, is volatile and could shift due to scandals involving Lulinha and lobbyist Roberta Luchsinger, which threaten the Bolsonaro ticket.

item.title: Datafolha mostra rejeição a Lula nos maiores colégios eleitorais
item.description: A Datafolha poll shows strong rejection of Lula's government in Brazil's largest electoral strongholds. In São Paulo, 48% rate the administration as bad or very bad, compared to 27% who consider it great or good, posing one of the main challenges to the president's reelection bid.

item.title: Lula tem 62% e Flávio, 29%, no 2º turno em PE, diz Datafolha
item.description: A Datafolha poll in Pernambuco shows Lula (PT) with a wide lead in the 2nd round, reaching 62% of voter intentions against 29% for Flávio Bolsonaro (PL). In the 1st round scenarios, Lula ranges between 55% and 56%, while Flávio remains at 24%, indicating strong polarization and the president's dominance in the state.

item.title: Datafolha: Lula tem 62% e Flávio 29% em Pernambuco no 2º turno
item.description: A Datafolha poll released on August 22 shows Lula (PT) with 62% versus 29% for Flávio Bolsonaro (PL) in a hypothetical runoff in Pernambuco, a 33-point lead. In the first round, Lula leads with 56% (without Marçal) or 55% (with Marçal), followed by Flávio at 24% in both scenarios. The survey interviewed 1,204 voters with a margin of error of three percentage points.

item.title: Rafael Fonteles tem 56% e venceria no 1º turno no Piauí, diz Datafolha
item.description: A Datafolha poll released on August 22, 2026, shows Piauí Governor Rafael Fonteles (PT) would win the state gubernatorial election in the first round with 56% of voting intentions. Joel Rodrigues (PP) is in second place with 21%, followed by several candidates with marginal percentages (1% to 2%). Blank/null votes account for 10%, and 5% of respondents did not know or did not answer. The survey interviewed 826 people, has a margin of error of 3 percentage points, and is registered with Brazil's Superior Electoral Court (TSE).

item.title: Lula tem 46% e Flávio 42% no 2º turno em MG, diz Datafolha
item.description: Datafolha poll released on Aug 22, 2026 shows a technical tie in Minas Gerais between Lula (46%) and Flávio Bolsonaro (42%) in a potential runoff, within the 3-point margin of error. In the first round, Lula leads with 37%, followed by Flávio (31%) and Zema (10%); a scenario including Pablo Marçal keeps Lula ahead at 36%.

item.title: Caiado muda de posição e diz ser a favor do fim da escala 6x1
item.description: Ronaldo Caiado (PSD), a presidential candidate, reversed his position on ending the 6x1 work schedule and declared himself in favor of the proposal during an event in Campinas, just three days after dismissing it as 'populist' and 'electioneering'. At the press conference he also called debate-avoiding rivals 'runaways'—without naming Lula or Flávio Bolsonaro—proposed a new crime category called 'domestic terrorism,' and pledged to build 40 maximum-security prisons with expanded use of artificial intelligence.

item.title: Datafolha: Flávio marca 47% contra 42% de Lula em SP no 2º turno; MG tem empate
item.description: A Datafolha poll shows Flávio Bolsonaro leading in São Paulo in a runoff with 47% versus Lula's 42%, a state representing 21% of Brazil's electorate. In Minas Gerais, there is a technical tie: Lula scores 46% and Flávio 42%, within the three-point margin of error. At the state level, Tarcísio leads in SP and Cleitinho Azevedo leads in MG.

item.title: Flávio tem 49% e Lula, 40%, no 2º turno no RJ, diz Datafolha
item.description: A Datafolha poll released on August 22, 2026, shows Senator Flávio Bolsonaro (PL) leading President Lula (PT) in a hypothetical 2nd round in Rio de Janeiro, with 49% versus 40%. In the 1st round, Flávio leads with 38% (with Pablo Marçal) or 41% (without Marçal), while Lula has 37% or 36%, respectively. The survey interviewed 1,204 voters, has a margin of error of 3 percentage points, and is registered with the TSE under number BR-08448/2026.

item.title: Cleitinho pede que PT não puna prefeita em MG que deseja apoiá-lo
item.description: Cleitinho Azevedo (Republicanos), candidate for governor of Minas Gerais, defended Mayor Jackeliny Nascimento of Frei Gaspar (PT), who publicly endorsed his campaign despite her party affiliation. The gesture could be considered party disloyalty, and the state PT directory, led by deputy Leninha, will review possible penalties. Cleitinho asked the PT not to punish the mayor and highlighted a parliamentary amendment he allocated to the municipality.

item.title: Filha do ministro aposentado do STF Ayres Britto se casa
item.description: Lawyer Nara Pinheiro Reis Ayres Britto, daughter of retired Supreme Court Justice Carlos Ayres Britto, married fellow attorney Bryan de Jongh Martins; both are partners at the Ayres Britto law firm founded by her father. Carlos Ayres Britto served on the Supreme Court from 2003 to 2012, was appointed by President Lula, presided over the Court and the Electoral Tribunal, and retired upon reaching the mandatory age of 70.

item.title: Lulinha planejou viagem para África e Europa com lobista, diz revista
item.description: A Veja magazine report revealed that messages recovered by the Federal Police show Fábio Luís Lula da Silva, known as Lulinha, and lobbyist Roberta Luchsinger planning trips to Africa and Paris in 2024, with an estimated cost of US$ 20,000 per person. In the messages, Luchsinger states she was researching the travel costs. The case involves indications of lobbying ties with the son of President Lula.

item.title: Datafolha: A vantagem de Flávio Bolsonaro sobre Lula no maior colégio eleitoral do país
item.description: A Datafolha poll conducted between August 18 and 21 in São Paulo shows Flávio Bolsonaro (PL) numerically ahead of Lula in the state: 37% to 33% in the first round and 47% to 42% in a hypothetical runoff, with the gap falling inside or outside the margin of error depending on the scenario. With Pablo Marçal included in the first round, Flávio and Lula are technically tied (35% to 34%). Lula's government is rated bad or very bad by 48% of São Paulo voters, while 27% rate it good or very good and 24% consider it average.

item.title: Flávio tem 51% e Lula, 39%, no 2º turno no DF, diz Datafolha
item.description: A Datafolha poll released on August 22, 2026 shows Senator Flávio Bolsonaro (PL) leading President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva (PT) 51% to 39% in a hypothetical 2nd round for the Presidency among voters in Brazil's Federal District. Blank/null votes total 9% and undecided voters 2%. In the 1st round, Flávio has 37% (or 39% without Pablo Marçal) and Lula 31%, followed by Ronaldo Caiado (9-10%). The survey interviewed 910 voters, with a 3-point margin of error and 95% confidence level.

item.title: Caiado chama de ‘fujões’ adversários que devem faltar a debates
item.description: Ronaldo Caiado (PSD) called potential debate absentees "fugitives," claiming those who avoid debates shouldn't even be allowed to register their candidacies. Romeu Zema (Novo) advocated for a new pension reform with contribution periods tied to life expectancy. Renan Santos (Missão) promised a "National Slum Eradication Framework" requiring an estimated R$1.3 to R$1.5 trillion over 10-15 years.

item.title: Datafolha: Flávio tem 47% contra 42% de Lula no 2º turno em SP
item.description: A Datafolha poll released on Aug 22, 2026 shows Senator Flávio Bolsonaro (PL) leading President Lula (PT) in a runoff among voters in São Paulo state, with 47% to 42% (blank/null 9%, undecided 1%). In the first round, Flávio leads with 37% and Lula has 33%, a scenario that remains similar even with Pablo Marçal in the race. The survey interviewed 1,610 voters, with a margin of error of 2 percentage points.

item.title: De olho nos evangélicos, Janja canta com cantor gospel em ato de Lula
item.description: At a campaign event in Rio, First Lady Janja sang the gospel jingle 'Tapete Vermelho' alongside pastor Kleber Lucas to court evangelical voters, a segment where Lula faces 62% disapproval. The PT is launching a National Evangelicals with Lula Committee, aiming to create over 1,000 grassroots committees nationwide, and is planning a dedicated evangelical rally in Rio.

item.title: Kalil alfineta Patrus após declaração sobre venda da Copasa
item.description: Alexandre Kalil (PDT), a candidate for the government of Minas Gerais, mocked his opponent Patrus Ananias (PT) after Patrus claimed, at a rally with President Lula, that he had voted against the sale of Copasa. Kalil pointed out that Patrus is a federal deputy, while votes on Copasa's denationalization take place in the state Legislative Assembly. Patrus acknowledged that re-nationalizing the company could take years due to economic and legal reasons.

item.title: Datafolha: Lula lidera em Minas e Flávio Bolsonaro é o 1º em São Paulo; veja os números
item.description: A Datafolha poll released on 08/22/2026 shows Flávio Bolsonaro (PL) leading Lula in a hypothetical second round in São Paulo (47% to 42%). In Minas Gerais, Lula leads by 46% to 42%. Nationally, Lula leads with 47% versus 43% for Flávio Bolsonaro.

item.title: Lula x Flávio: A diferença na intenção de votos nos dois maiores colégios eleitorais, segundo o Datafolha
item.description: A Datafolha poll reveals contrasting scenarios in Brazil's two largest electoral strongholds: in São Paulo, Flávio Bolsonaro leads Lula in a runoff 47% to 42%, a gap beyond the margin of error. In Minas Gerais, Lula is numerically ahead 46% to 42%, but statistically tied. The survey also shows Tarcísio de Freitas in a strong position for the São Paulo gubernatorial race.

item.title: Flávio Bolsonaro mostra visão ultrapassada sobre energia ao falar sobre E32, diz Mercadante
item.description: Petrobras president Mercadante criticized Flávio Bolsonaro's claim that "gasoline became ethanol" as mistaken and climate-denialist. According to him, the statement reflects an outdated view of Brazil's energy matrix and the role of biofuels.

item.title: Datafolha em PE: Lula, 56%; Flávio Bolsonaro, 24%; Ronaldo Caiado; 2%; Renan Santos; 2%; Zema, 1%; Augusto Cury, 1%
item.description: A Datafolha poll released on August 22 shows Lula leading the presidential race with 56% of voting intentions in the first round, followed by Flávio Bolsonaro with 24%. In the scenario including Pablo Marçal, the numbers remain virtually unchanged, with Lula at 55% and Flávio at 24%. In the second round, Lula extends his lead to 62% against 29% for Flávio Bolsonaro, while federal government approval reaches 62% of the population.

item.title: Datafolha no DF: Flávio Bolsonaro, 39%; Lula, 31%; Ronaldo Caiado; 10%; Renan Santos; 3%; Zema, 2%; Augusto Cury, 1%
item.description: A Datafolha poll in the Federal District shows Flávio Bolsonaro leading the presidential race with 39% of voting intentions, followed by Lula with 31% and Ronaldo Caiado with 10%. In the scenario including Pablo Marçal, Flávio maintains his lead with 37%, with no significant changes in the overall picture. In a potential runoff, Flávio has 51% against Lula's 43% among DF voters.

item.title: Datafolha em SP: Flávio Bolsonaro, 37%; Lula, 33%; Renan, 5%
item.description: A Datafolha poll in São Paulo state shows Flávio Bolsonaro (PL) leading the presidential race with 37% of voting intentions, against 33% for Lula (PT), in a scenario without Pablo Marçal. In a runoff, Flávio would expand his lead to 47% to 42%. Disapproval of Lula's government reaches 56% among São Paulo voters, with 48% rating it as bad or terrible.

item.title: Datafolha em MG: Lula, 37%; Flávio Bolsonaro, 31%; Zema, 10%
item.description: A Datafolha poll in Minas Gerais shows Lula (PT) leading with 37%, followed by Flávio Bolsonaro (PL) at 31%, within the 3-point margin of error. Romeu Zema (Novo) is third with 10%. In a scenario including Pablo Marçal, Lula drops to 36%, Flávio remains at 31%, and Marçal gets 4%.

item.title: “Marginais têm até dezembro para meter o pé do Brasil”, diz Flávio
item.description: Senator Flávio Bolsonaro (PL), presidential pre-candidate, stated he intends to declare war on criminal factions if elected, giving a deadline of December for 'criminals' to leave Brazil. The statement was made during the launch of Douglas Ruas's candidacy for the governorship of Rio de Janeiro. Flávio plans to classify groups such as Comando Vermelho, PCC, and militias as terrorist organizations.

item.title: Justiça da Bolívia mantém prisão preventiva de ex-assessor de Milei
item.description: A Bolivian court extended the preventive detention of Argentine Fernando Cerimedo, a former advisor to Javier Milei's campaign and current advisor to Bolivian President Rodrigo Paz, for another 180 days. He is suspected of orchestrating a shooting attack against his ex-girlfriend, Bolivian lawyer Nadia Beller, in Santa Cruz de la Sierra, based on cell phone messages obtained by prosecutors. In Brazil, Cerimedo had been indicted by the Federal Police in 2024 in the investigation into the attempted coup in favor of Bolsonaro, but was never formally charged.

item.title: Renan promete R$ 1,5 trilhão para “desfavelização” em até 15 anos
item.description: Presidential candidate Renan Santos (Missão) unveiled the 'National Favela Eradication Framework' in São Paulo, proposing R$ 1.5 trillion in investments over 10–15 years to renovate housing, legalize properties, and install infrastructure in favelas without displacing residents. Funding would come from public and private investment, 'favela eradication bonds,' and cuts to tax exemptions, public-sector 'supersalaries,' and public debt interest, with at least R$ 100 billion per year starting in the fifth year.

item.title: Como está disputa Lula x Flávio, segundo as pesquisas desta semana
item.description: Polls released this week by Datafolha and BTG/Nexus show a technical tie between Lula and Flávio Bolsonaro in a hypothetical runoff, with the president numerically ahead (47% to 43% in Datafolha; 47% to 44% in BTG/Nexus) but within the two-point margin of error. In the first round, Lula also leads numerically in both surveys, with 39% (Datafolha) and 41% (BTG/Nexus), against Flávio's 33% and 36%, respectively. The data indicate stability compared to previous polls.

item.title: Os destinos discutidos pelo grupo de Lulinha para guardar dinheiro fora do Brasil
item.description: A Federal Police investigation revealed that the group linked to Fábio Luís Lula da Silva (Lulinha) and lobbyist Roberta Luchsinger discussed opening companies and bank accounts in Liechtenstein and Switzerland to shield assets. According to seized messages, Roberta claimed it was 'impossible to seize' funds held in the principality, a former tax haven. The scheme is suspected of influence peddling and selling access to the federal government.

item.title: Lulistas e bolsonaristas veem adversários como mais radicais do que eles são, diz estudo
item.description: A study by More in Common/Ipsos-Ipec shows that Lula and Bolsonaro supporters hold distorted views of each other, perceiving the opposing side as more radical than it actually is. The survey, conducted with 2,000 people across 130 Brazilian municipalities, identified a 'perception gap' on both sides: Bolsonaro supporters are more favorable to social mobility, wage equality, and democracy than Lula supporters imagine, while Lula supporters agree more with conservative ideas about crime, income, and family than Bolsonaro supporters assume. The largest gap concerns wage equality between men and women, where Bolsonaro supporters gave an average score of 94, but Lula supporters estimated only 73.

item.title: Lula afirma năo ter preferęncia entre países e quer construir parcerias em minerais críticos
item.description: President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva (PT), running for reelection, stated this Saturday, the 22nd, that Brazil is open to building partnerships with various countries in the critical minerals sector, without showing preference among nations. The statement reinforces the government's interest in expanding international cooperation in this strategic area.

item.title: Toffoli fecha as portas para mais um habeas corpus que tentava soltar Bolsonaro
item.description: Supreme Court Justice Dias Toffoli rejected another appeal (agravo regimental) seeking to reopen a habeas corpus petition to free former President Jair Bolsonaro, who is serving a 27-year, three-month sentence for leading the attempted coup. Toffoli stated the case had already been sent back and that third parties cannot interfere in the defense, as Bolsonaro has officially appointed lawyers. The justice also denied requests to recuse other ministers from the coup case.

item.title: Vida de Lulinha na Espanha é “bem modesta”, diz Quaquá
item.description: Washington Quaquá, mayor of Maricá and PT vice-president, once again defended Fábio Luís Lula da Silva (Lulinha), describing his life in Spain as 'quite modest,' despite reports that the son of President Lula lives in a luxury condominium near Madrid with a high rent. The statement follows new information published by Metrópoles about the businessman's lifestyle abroad.

item.title: Em eventos de campanha no Rio, Lula promete reforço na segurança e Flávio propőe 'guerra' a facçőes
item.description: During campaign events in Rio de Janeiro, President Lula (PT) promised to strengthen public security by sending a constitutional amendment to recreate the Ministry of Public Security and bolster the Federal Police and Highway Police, in addition to expanding the imprisonment of criminal factions. Flávio Bolsonaro (PL), a presidential candidate, proposed declaring 'war' on 'narco-terrorists,' classifying groups like the Red Command and PCC as narco-terrorist organizations. Both also addressed topics such as education and social security in their events.

item.title: Os ex-BBBs mais ricos a se candidatarem nas eleições de 2026
item.description: Six former BBB contestants run in the 2026 elections. Vivian Amorim (Uniao Brasil/AM) leads with R$3.4 million in assets, followed by Adrilles Jorge (Uniao Brasil/SP) with R$540k. Lucas Penteado (SP) declares only R$1,200.

item.title: PT publica foto de comício de Lula em BH e provoca Flávio: 'Chora não'
item.description: The PT posted on X a photo of Lula at a rally in Belo Horizonte during Patrus Ananias' gubernatorial campaign launch, provoking Senator Flávio Bolsonaro with the phrase 'Chora não'. The move aims to bolster PT's presence in Minas Gerais and counter the PL.

item.title: Lula: escolha em 2026 é sobre quem quer vender as praias e quem quer o povo nelas
item.description: Lula launched his re-election campaign in Rio de Janeiro with a speech contrasting those who want to sell the beaches (privatization) with those who want the people in them (public management). He emphasizes valuing public space and popular access as the core of his platform.

item.title: No Rio, Lula promete Ministério da Segurança e tirar bandidos de territórios
item.description: Lula promised to create a Ministry of Public Security and remove criminals from territories dominated by organized crime during his first campaign event in Rio de Janeiro alongside Eduardo Paes. He defended his alliance with Paes and praised Ricardo Couto for political 'cleaning' in the state, while Paes linked organized crime in politics to PL candidates.

item.title: Zema defende nova reforma da Previdência e aumento da contribuição
item.description: Romeu Zema advocated for a new Social Security reform that increases contribution time based on life expectancy, aiming to prevent deficits and safeguard already acquired rights, especially for new workers.

item.title: Em jingle, Zema fala em 'acabar com PT', mostra ministros do STF na cadeia e Virgínia surpresa
item.description: Novo candidate Romeu Zema released a campaign jingle pledging to end the PT and depicting STF ministers in prison. The ad adopts an aggressive tone targeting both the party and the Supreme Court.

item.title: Lulinha e Dark Horse trazem PF e Mendonça para a disputa eleitoral
item.description: Federal Police investigations involving Lulinha (Lula's son) and financing of the "Dark Horse" film about Bolsonaro put Supreme Court Justice André Mendonça at the center of the 2026 election race. Lulinha faces three inquiries for alleged influence peddling and corruption at the Health Ministry, while PF probes a R$61 million transfer from Banco Master to the documentary. Datafolha poll shows Lula at 47% vs 43% for Flávio Bolsonaro in a hypothetical runoff, within the margin of error.

item.title: Zema lança jingle de forró com vídeo que mostra Lula e ministros presos
item.description: Romeu Zema released a forró campaign jingle and AI-generated animation depicting Lula and STF ministers as prisoners. The satirical video 'Untouchables' shows Gilmar Mendes, Dias Toffoli, and Alexandre de Moraes dancing in a jail cell, reinforcing criticism of the three branches of government. The piece ends with Zema wearing the presidential sash and receiving news of a police operation against Lula and his son.

item.title: Vice-presidente do PT minimiza luxos de Lulinha: "Pequeno empresário"
item.description: PT Vice-President Washington Quaquá downplayed the luxury of Lulinha’s Madrid condo, calling the rent typical for a small Brazilian businessman. He criticized the overuse of police investigations in politics and argued the scandal will have minimal impact on Lula’s campaign.

item.title: Zema chama João Campos de “intocável das bets” por reduzir imposto
item.description: Romeu Zema criticized João Campos for lowering the service tax on sports betting in Recife to 2%, calling him the 'untouchable of bets' and vowing to ban the industry if elected president. Campos justified the tax cut as necessary to prevent revenue loss to other cities.
